findings.title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in UI
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. Unlike the `disconnectMutation` right below it (which invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`), nothing invalidates the `connectedCalendars` query after the cache rows are deleted. The `cacheUpdatedAt` value that drives `hasCache` comes from that query, so unless the parent happens to pass an `onChanged` that refetches, the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated ..." and the "Delete cached data" entry for cache that no longer exists (and the query is configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, so it won't self-correct). Add `onSettled: () => utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` to the delete mutation, mirroring the disconnect mutation.

findings.title: Authorization failure thrown as plain Error becomes a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
findings.body: When the credential does not belong to the caller, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps non-`TRPCError` exceptions to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, so a legitimate not-found/forbidden case is reported to the client as a server failure and will be logged/alerted as an unexpected error. Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or `FORBIDDEN`). Additionally, the existence check uses `prisma.credential.findFirst` with no `select`, pulling the full row including the OAuth `key` blob just to test existence; `select: { id: true }` is sufficient.

findings.title: Unused extra UPDATE of all SelectedCalendar rows on every cache refresh/webhook
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now ends with `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`, an UPDATE of every SelectedCalendar row for the credential solely to bump `@updatedAt`. This runs on every Google push notification (which can arrive in bursts) and on the unwatch path. The PR description itself states the resulting `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not consumed anywhere—the UI reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt` instead. This is dead write traffic that also makes `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` meaningless as a "record changed" signal. Remove it (along with the now-unneeded `updateManyByCredentialId` helper) or wire it to an actual consumer.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars type tightened to require fields the function never uses
findings.body: `UserWithCalendars.allSelectedCalendars` / `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` in addition to `externalId | integration | eventTypeId`, but nothing in `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` reads those fields. This forces every caller (tRPC session user, API v2 via `@calcom/platform-libraries`, tests constructing users) to supply them—hence the otherwise unrelated change to `findUnlockedUserForSession` in `packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts` that now selects `googleChannelId` into the session user. Any external caller that builds a user object with the previous minimal shape will fail type-checking for no functional reason. Revert the type widening and the session select change.

findings.title: Cache timestamp formatted with hard-coded en-US locale, ignoring user locale/timezone
findings.body: The "Last updated" timestamp is rendered via `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, so non-English users see US date ordering (MM/DD/YY) and 12-hour time regardless of their configured locale, and the time is in the browser timezone rather than the user's profile timezone used elsewhere in the app. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (e.g. `i18n.language`) and/or the existing dayjs helpers with the user's timezone.

findings.title: Backfill sets updatedAt of all existing cache rows to migration time, producing misleading 'Last updated' values
findings.body: `ALTER TABLE "CalendarCache" ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" ... DEFAULT NOW()` stamps every pre-existing cache row with the moment the migration ran. The new UI surfaces this value as "Last updated: {{timestamp}}", so for all existing users the cache will appear freshly refreshed at deploy time even if it is weeks old. Since `expiresAt` is always written as `updatedAt + 30 days` by `upsertCachedAvailability`, a more accurate backfill is available: add `UPDATE "CalendarCache" SET "updatedAt" = "expiresAt" - INTERVAL '30 days';` after the ALTER. Also the retained Prisma warning comment ("without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty") is no longer accurate for this hand-edited SQL.

findings.title: Dev script is macOS-only (`sed -i ''`) and writes .env relative to CWD, not the repo
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD sed syntax; on GNU sed (Linux CI/dev boxes) the empty string is taken as the script and the substitution expression as a filename, so the command fails with "can't read ...: No such file". Separately, `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory rather than the script location, so running `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root (the natural invocation) creates/edits a `.env` one level above the repository. Resolve paths from `$(dirname "$0")` and use a portable in-place edit. This file (and the `dev:cron` change in apps/web/package.json) is also unrelated to the cache-status feature and would be better split out.

findings.title: dev:cron now relies on `npx tsx`, which is not a declared dependency
findings.body: The `dev:cron` script was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not listed in `dependencies`/`devDependencies` (while `ts-node` still is). `npx` will fetch an arbitrary latest `tsx` at runtime, making the script non-reproducible and failing offline. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it directly, or keep `ts-node`. This change is also unrelated to the PR's feature.

findings.title: No tests for the new deleteCache mutation, cache-status repository method, or dropdown rendering
findings.body: The PR adds an authorization-sensitive destructive mutation (`deleteCacheHandler`), a new repository query (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` with `groupBy`/`_max`), enrichment logic in `connectedCalendarsHandler`, and a UI component that replaces the existing `DisconnectIntegration` trash button with an ellipsis dropdown, yet no unit, integration, or e2e tests are added or updated. At minimum there should be a test asserting a user cannot delete cache for a credential they don't own, a test that `cacheUpdatedAt` is attached to the right credential (and null when no rows exist), and a check that existing Playwright flows which previously clicked the direct disconnect button still pass with the new two-step dropdown interaction. The PR description notes end-to-end verification was not performed locally.
